entities.summary:
Leo II or Leon II was king of the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia, ruling from 1269/1270 to 1289. He was the son of King Hetoum I and Queen Isabella and was a member of the House of Lampron.

Born in 1248, Leo II ascended to the throne after his father's death in 1269/1270. His reign was marked by conflicts with the Mamluk Sultanate and the Mongol Empire, as well as internal power struggles within the kingdom. Leo II implemented various administrative reforms and strengthened the kingdom's military, but his rule was ultimately cut short by his death on February 6, 1289.

Leo II's legacy is complex and multifaceted. He played a significant role in shaping the Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia's foreign policy, particularly in his dealings with the Mamluk Sultanate. His reign also saw significant cultural and economic developments, including the establishment of trade routes and the promotion of Christianity.

Despite his relatively short reign, Leo II's impact on Armenian history was substantial. He laid the groundwork for future leaders, who would go on to shape the kingdom's destiny in the centuries that followed.

The Armenian Kingdom of Cilicia's history is often overshadowed by more prominent regional powers, but Leo II's accomplishments demonstrate the importance of this medieval kingdom in the broader context of world history.
